subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Tail Risk and Fat Tails
description: One-minute skill: Tail Risk and Fat Tails.

hook.text: Normal distribution says extreme events are nearly impossible. Financial markets prove this wrong repeatedly.

buildup.text: Tail Risk and Fat Tails sets up the tradeoffs, the uncertainty, and the decision pressure.

discovery.text: Financial returns have fat tails: extreme events happen far more often than bell curves predict.

twist.text: Long-Term Capital Management used normal distribution models. It lost $4.6 billion in weeks when fat-tail events struck.

climax.text: Tail Risk and Fat Tails matters because structure beats guesswork when stakes are high.

punchline.text: Extreme events happen more than models predict.

quiz.question: What are 'fat tails' in finance?
options: Extreme events occurring far more frequently than normal distribution models predict
